subject: Privacy: SynthWorks DPA - telemetry, embeddings, and e-sign execution

Subject: Fwd: SynthWorks initial DPA redline - telemetry & embeddings

Quick ask: can we align on one internal position on controller vs processor for embeddings/logs and a hardline on telemetry retention before I send consolidated redline back?

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-11 10:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: SynthWorks initial DPA redline - telemetry & embeddings

Thanks for the forward, Priya. I reviewed the customer's redline. High-level thoughts:

- Controller/Processor: We should preserve the standard position: Redwood acts as processor for customer-provided content and derived artifacts; customer remains controller. For embeddings we propose language that treats embeddings as "derivative, pseudonymized outputs" generated in the course of processing — processor-held but controller's responsibility for any inputs that qualify as personal data.

- Telemetry/logs: Counter-propose a 30-day default retention for request-level telemetry (raw request/response pairs), with aggregation and metrics retained longer (12 months) in aggregated, non-identifiable form. Add explicit encryption and access-limited clause. The customer's 90-day ask is high; stick to 30 days unless they can justify.

- Transfers: We should require SCCs + our Processor Addendum. If they push back, offer standard EU SCCs + narrower transfer purpose. Avoid claiming controller status over logs.

I'll draft specific clause text (controller/processor and telemetry excerpt) and push to the redline. Marissa, will you check DocuSign mechanics and any contracting implications if we must be co-controller for any reason?

-Laura
Legal Counsel

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11 15:20 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: SynthWorks initial DPA redline - telemetry & embeddings

Adding technical detail for legal to use in the clause:

- "Telemetry/logs": we should define this narrowly as (a) service infrastructure logs (GPU metrics, scheduling, X) and (b) request-level tracing (request id, timestamp, latency). We should explicitly exclude stored model artifacts and KV cache contents unless customer opts in.

- "Embeddings": by default embeddings are non-reversible vectors; however reversibility depends on prompt/data. Recommend we add: "Customer acknowledges that embeddings may contain personal data if provided in the input and agrees to treat embeddings derived from such inputs as personal data under applicable law." This pushes controller obligations to the customer while allowing us to assert processor status for handling and storage.

- Technical safeguards: AES-256 at rest, TLS1.2+ in transit, access logs, and auditability. Set retention for raw request payloads to 30 days; derived metrics can be 12 months. Include an option for customers to request shorter retention via config.

I'll attach a short telemetry mapping spreadsheet for the clauses (see Telemetry_Mapping.xlsx).

-Rishi
Head of Privacy Engineering

Thanks for sending the initial DPA. We've completed an internal review and attached a consolidated redline (SynthWorks_DPA_Redline_v3.pdf) that contains: (1) proposed controller/processor language for embeddings, (2) a telemetry handling excerpt (30-day raw retention / 12-month aggregated metrics), (3) SCCs + Processor Addendum reference, and (4) updated subprocessor list.

Action items for your team:
- Please review the consolidated redline and confirm whether the embeddings clause meets your controller expectations.
- Confirm acceptance of SCCs + our processor addendum (link in the attachment).
- Provide any missing subprocessors you require us to disclose (we've included our current list; will update if any changes).

We can send for e-sign via DocuSign once the redline is agreed. I'm also sharing HubSpot link to the deal so procurement can coordinate timelines: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/48729/SW-2027-042-PRIV

DocuSign envelope will be prepared after your confirmation; please flag any required signatories.

Best,

From: Marta Lopez <marta.legal@synthworks.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12 13:05 -0700
Subject: Re: SynthWorks DPA - consolidated redline and next steps (DocuSign prep)

Thanks, Priya — we appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifying questions before we can sign:

1) Embeddings reversibility: can Redwood provide a short technical note or assurance on whether embeddings are reversible in your standard pipeline? Our security team needs specifics to evaluate risk.
2) Controller designation: your proposal still reads like you are a processor, but we need confirmation on who is the controller for derived telemetry that may include user identifiers (e.g., request ids tied to customer user IDs).
3) Subprocessors & Evidence: please confirm the updated subprocessor list and share SOC2 report / summary.

If the answers are acceptable we can move to e-sign; target procurement timeline is EOD 2027-04-14.

-Marta
Senior Counsel, SynthWorks Inc.

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.legal@synthworks.com>, Ethan Cole <ethan@synthworks.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-13 16:05 -0700
Subject: Re: SynthWorks DPA - consolidated redline and next steps (DocuSign prep)

Hi Marta — quick answers inline below and attaching the SOC2 summary: SOC2_summary.pdf.

On 1) Embeddings reversibility: As Rishi indicated, embeddings generated by our standard encoder are non-reversible by design (they are high-dimensional vectors with no deterministic mapping to original text). That said, reversibility risk increases if the input itself contains small, unique identifiers; we recommend that customers avoid sending direct identifiers in prompts. We will provide a 1-page technical note (I asked Rishi to draft) that you can share with security.

On 2) Controller designation: Customer remains the controller for inputs and any derived data that can be linked back to an identified person. Redwood is the processor for generation, storage, and transmission of embeddings and telemetry. For request-level telemetry that includes customer user IDs, we propose a narrow carve-out: Redwood stores request IDs for operational debugging but will not map them to customer identities except under documented support processes. We'll include a clause that requires a customer-signed request for re-identification support.

On 3) Subprocessors & evidence: current subprocessors list is in the redline. SOC2_summary.pdf attached and our compliance page link is in the Drive folder.

If legal sign-off looks good (Laura / Marissa), I'll prepare the DocuSign envelope and send to your signatories. We can meet the EOD 2027-04-14 procurement target if we get the green light today.

Thanks — Priya
--
